body: @rzvn01 Could you please enable debug logging for both the AMF and UDM, reproduce the issue, and share the logs so I can investigate the root cause?

[udm-report-logs-2026-10-01.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32896013/udm-report-logs-2026-10-01.zip)

I went back and reproduced this with the AMF and UDM at debug, first on the same versions as in the report, then on
2.8.0. Logs are in the zip.

**In short:** the pool does fill up, but I got the reason wrong. Most subscriptions are released normally. What stays
behind are the UEs whose release got aborted by an SBI error during the burst right after the RAN is killed. On 2.7.5
that was about 30 % of a 500-UE batch every time I killed the emulator. On 2.8.0 the same test ran clean for all 500.
Three things I wrote were wrong: it's 2 subscriptions per UE, not 8, they are reclaimed by implicit deregistration, and
the AMF does log errors.

**Setup:** Open5GS 2.7.5 (`gradiant/open5gs:2.7.5` for all NFs), UDM with its default config (no `global.max.ue`, so
the pool is 1024 × 4 = 4096), AMF and UDM at `debug`. PacketRusher (`gradiant/packetrusher:5bf8b4e`) as the RAN, 500
UEs, 50 ms stagger, one PDU session each. Single-node Kubernetes. Then the exact same run with every image on 2.8.0
and nothing else changed.

**Test:** register 500 UEs, kill the emulator (no deregistration), 180 s later register the same 500 again, kill again,
wait 35 minutes. I counted every `POST` and `DELETE` on `.../sdm-subscriptions` per SUPI in the UDM log, and used the
`callbackReference` in the body to tell the AMF from the SMF.

**2.7.5:**

1. Each UE gets 2 subscriptions: one from the AMF at registration, one from the SMF when the PDU session is set up. The
   pool is `max.ue * MAX_NUM_OF_UDM_SDM_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_UE` (4), so 4096 is enough for 2048 UEs like these.
2. Re-registering inside the window doesn't add anything. The SMF deletes its old subscription and makes a new one (500
   deleted, 500 created), the AMF keeps its own. Still 2 per UE.
3. Implicit deregistration works where it gets to run: `Mobile Reachable Timer Expired` 780 s after the kill (T3512
   540 s + 240 s), `Implicit De-registered` 780 s after that, and then the AMF unsubscribes and releases the SM context,
   so the SMF unsubscribes too. 335 UEs went through that and all their subscriptions were deleted.
4. What stays behind:
   - When the emulator dies, the SCTP association drops, the AMF removes the gNB and sends an SM context update
     (`upCnxState: DEACTIVATED`) for every UE in one burst. For 156 of 500 at the first kill and 143 of 500 at the
     second, the send failed (`[sbi] WARNING: Send failure: Connection reset by peer`, `ogs_sbi_client_handler() failed`).
     The AMF then tries to send a NAS message to the UE (`DL NAS transport`, `nas_5gs_send_back_gsm_message`), hits
     `[amf] ERROR: gNB has already been removed`, and gives up (`Cannot receive SBI message`,
     `amf_state_operational: Expectation 'r == OGS_OK' failed`). Those UEs never go to CM-IDLE, no mobile reachable
     timer is started, and their two subscriptions stay. The 143 SUCIs in those warnings are exactly the 143 IMSIs that
     never got a timer expiry. The first 156 only got cleaned up because the same UEs registered again 180 s later.
   - In the implicit deregistration burst (357 UEs in the same second) 22 more failed the same way: after the UECM
     PATCH the SBI call failed (16 `Connection reset by peer`, 6 `SBI transaction has already been removed`) and the
     deregistration ended with `[amf] ERROR: NG context has already been removed (nas-path.c:975)`, SM context and SMF
     subscription still there. The SCP logged `Connection timer expired` on some of the `sm-contexts/{ref}/release`
     calls in that burst.
   - After 35 minutes: 165 of 500 UEs still in the AMF, 324 of their subscriptions still in the UDM, and only a
     restart clears them. That's what filled the pool in my original runs (batches of up to 1000 UEs, each killed,
     within 80 minutes).

**2.8.0:** both kills went through for all 500 UEs with no SBI error (500 updates sent and answered each time, 0
resets). `Mobile Reachable Timer Expired` 500 of 500, `Implicit De-registered` 500 of 500. 1506 subscriptions created,
1500 deleted, 6 left (the two UERANSIM UEs that stay registered on my testbed). Nothing left behind. The SBI errors that
start the whole thing on 2.7.5 just didn't happen on 2.8.0 in this test, so I can't tell from it what 2.8.0 does if
they do happen.

**About the AMF logging nothing:** I was wrong there. It does log the ERROR lines above when the gNB goes away. What it
doesn't do is link them to the `5GS services not allowed` rejects that come later from the full UDM pool.

**Closing:** since it doesn't reproduce on 2.8.0, closing is fine with me. One thing I'd like your opinion on: in
`amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context` the non-2xx branch still answers the RAN (`nas_5gs_send_gsm_reject` /
`ngap_send_error_indication2`) and returns `OGS_ERROR`. If an update after a gNB loss fails on the SBI side on current
code, is there anything that releases that UE later, or would it stay held like on 2.7.5?

Attached: `run6` (2.7.5) and `run7` (2.8.0). The 2.7.5 SMF log is missing (lost when I switched versions), the 2.8.0
one is there.
